title: What If Your Only Way to Call for Help Was a Pigeon? In 1918 It Was

scenes.text: What if your last hope of rescue was a pigeon? In 1918, 550 soldiers had only that.
October 4th. An American battalion was surrounded in a French forest, and its own artillery began shelling it.
The last pigeon went up with a note: our own artillery is dropping a barrage on us. For heaven's sake, stop it.
The story goes that Cher Ami was shot through the chest and still flew 25 miles in 25 minutes.
Only 194 men walked out. The pigeon lost a leg, won a French medal, and is in the Smithsonian.
In 2021, a DNA test showed the famous hen was male. And historians still can't prove it was this bird.

description:
What if a pigeon was the only way to call for help? In October 1918 the men of the Lost Battalion, about 554 American soldiers surrounded in the Argonne forest, were down to their last bird while their own artillery shelled them.
The message read: we are along the road parallel to 276.4. Our own artillery is dropping a barrage directly on us. For heaven's sake, stop it. The homing pigeon Cher Ami is credited with carrying it 25 miles in about 25 minutes despite a chest wound and a shattered leg; 194 men walked out. The bird received the French Croix de Guerre, died in June 1919 and is displayed at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History, where a 2021 DNA test showed it was male. Historians caution that nothing conclusively links this pigeon to that message.
